items.title: Forge: friendly merge errors (no raw xelib/EPERM dumps) + cleanup hardening
items.why: a real tester saw a raw 'EPERM … Loader failed' dump on the Forge's plugin list instead of a nice message — the worker's raw stderr leaks straight to the UI; also harden the non-fatal sandbox cleanup (their C:-drive Steam install invites Defender file locks).
items.prompt: Read vortex-tools/vortex-collection-tools/design/BUILD-PROMPT-merge-error-handling.md and build it. A tester saw a raw EPERM sandbox-cleanup warning + xelib 'Loader failed' verbatim on the Forge instead of a friendly error. (1) Tag the removeSandbox cleanup warning `##WARN## ` in merge-worker.js and have merge-runner.js SKIP those lines like it already skips `##PROGRESS## ` — the non-fatal cleanup warning must NEVER reach the user. (2) Mark ONLY the worker's own intentional friendly errors with a `##USERERR## ` prefix; in merge-runner.js surface those verbatim and fall back to the existing CRASH_HELP_TEXT for ALL other stderr (native xelib errors, unmarked crashes) — defensive by default; keep raw text in a console.error. (3) Harden removeSandbox: maxRetries 5→10, retryDelay 200→300, and best-effort-sweep leftover .vct-merge-tmp/vct-merge-* dirs on the next run. Use the EXISTING CRASH_HELP_TEXT copy (design-owned) — don't invent new user-facing text; flag in the handoff if a case genuinely needs its own message. Verify + handoff.

items.title: ESLifier awareness — Settings path + Missing Masters downgrade
items.why: kills the false-positive 'missing master' when ESLifier deliberately swapped a file
items.prompt: Read vortex-tools/vortex-collection-tools/design/BUILD-PROMPT-eslifier-filter.md and build it. CRITICAL: verify the detection against a real ESLifier output folder + a live Missing Masters scan FIRST (disabled-count lesson) — don't ship a guessed trace. v1 = Settings ESLifier output-folder path + Nexus helper link, and the Missing Masters ON-by-default toggle that downgrades ESLifier-traced files from critical to warning (surfaced, not hidden). Update config.example.json for both new fields. Handoff with what the real ESLifier→Vortex deploy actually looked like and which scan signal the false positive fired on.

items.title: Clear stale end-of-flow banner on Preview re-arm
items.prompt: In Update Collection: re-doing Apply Ignores via Preview doesn't clear the stale end-of-flow completion banner until Apply re-succeeds. Wire callout-clearing into the Preview re-arm so the banner clears the moment the step is re-armed. Pre-existing minor issue; not blocking.

items.title: New tool: Rebuild Missing Files — check picked collections, fix only what's actually missing
items.why: Full Rebuild Collection is overkill when only a handful of files are actually missing from staging — this checks one or more collections, shows exactly what's missing per mod, and fixes just those.
items.prompt:
NEW TOOL, mockup-approved. Read `design/vortex-rebuild-missing-files-mockup.html` (title tag: "Approved ✓ 2026-08-05") FIRST — it's the exact visual/copy/interaction spec for both screens (collection picker, scan report). Copy its markup/CSS classes into the real page per DESIGN.md's own standing rule ("start by copying an existing report's markup, not designing from a blank page") — this mockup already did that copying from the Archive Finder results-table pattern, so it should translate almost directly.

MOTIVATION (director's own words): 'I've run into the issue where I wonder why something in game is not working and every time, some or all of the files are missing from the staging folder — having to rebuild collection for all collections isn't feasible when only a small number of files might be missing.' This tool checks one or more picked collections for missing staging files and lets the user fix just those, without a full Rebuild Collection pass.

REUSABLE PIECES ALREADY CONFIRMED IN THE CODEBASE — don't reinvent these:
- `lib/sevenzip.js`'s `listArchive(exePath, archivePath)` (line 80) — lists an archive's real contents WITHOUT extracting, already used by `rebuild-mod.js:115`. This is the cheap check: for each mod, list its archive's contents and check each entry's existence under the mod's own staging folder (`path.join(stagingDir, targetFolderName, internalPath)`) via `fs.existsSync`. No extraction needed for the SCAN step.
- `lib/sevenzip.js`'s `extractMany(exePath, archivePath, internalPaths, destDir)` (line 124) — extracts a SPECIFIC list of archive members in one 7z call, preserving their internal paths. This is exactly the FIX action: call it with just the missing internalPaths, `destDir` = the mod's own staging folder. No new extraction logic to write.
- `/api/collections` + `/api/workshop-collections` routes (see `web/rebuild-routes.js` and the Workshop-tab concept in `TECHNICAL.md:540-573`) already supply the data for the collection picker — Nexus/installed vs. Workshop-authoring collections are already a distinguished, well-documented concept, not something to invent.
- `web/run-state.js`'s SSE bookkeeping (the same mechanism `rebuild-routes.js`'s `/plan`/`/runs` endpoints already use) — reuse it for both the scan's own progress stream and the fix-action's progress stream, rather than building new plumbing.
- `lib/collection-runner.js`'s existing multi-collection-tolerant scan-merge pattern (`{ results, workshopOnlyCollections }` shape in `lib/vortex-sync/lib.js:200-218`) — one bad/unreadable collection shouldn't lose the other picked collections' results; follow the same tolerance pattern.

GENUINELY NEW WORK:
1. **Scan engine** (new function, e.g. in a new `lib/missing-files-scan.js` or alongside `collection-runner.js` — your call on placement, flag it in the handoff): for each picked collection, read its `collection.json`, and for each mod: resolve its archive (same archive-resolution logic `classifyMod` already does, `lib/rebuild-mod.js:66` — don't duplicate, extract/reuse if it's cleanly separable, or call into it), `listArchive` it, and diff entries against what's actually on disk in that mod's staging folder. Collect missing-file lists per mod, grouped by collection.
2. **New routes** (e.g. `web/rebuild-missing-routes.js`, mirroring `rebuild-routes.js`'s own `/plan` → `/runs` shape): a scan endpoint (POST, takes picked collection IDs, streams progress via SSE, returns the missing-files report) and a fix endpoint (POST, takes a list of {collectionId, modId} to fix, streams progress, calls `extractMany` per mod, falls back to Download-archive-then-extract if the archive itself isn't on disk — reuse whatever Rebuild Collection's own download-missing-archive logic already does).
3. **New page + client JS** (`web/public/rebuild-missing-*` or wherever this project's own naming convention puts a new tool — check an existing tool's file layout, e.g. Archive Finder's, before choosing) implementing both mockup screens: collection picker (multi-select cards, Nexus + Workshop groups) → scan report (select-all/invert-selection/clear-selection, per-mod row with missing-file count pill + collapsed file list + Extract-from-archive/Open-staging-folder/Download-archive-if-needed row actions).
4. **Home page entry point** — add this tool to wherever the app's own tool launcher/home page lists tools (`web/public/` home view), matching the existing tool-card visual pattern (`design/vortex-home-mockup.html` if that's the reference).

CRITICAL, per this project's own established discipline for exactly this class of feature (same lesson as the ESLifier/Missing Masters false-positive incident): verify the scan's own missing-file detection against a REAL collection with REAL known-missing files first, before trusting it. Don't ship a guessed diff.

VOICE: run all new user-facing copy through `plain-language-writer` — casual register for the picker/report UI, serious register for the extract/fix action (it writes to the staging folder, matching this project's own established registry of 'genuinely consequential' actions).

VERIFY: a real scan + real fix against an actual collection with genuinely missing staging files (delete a few files from a real mod's staging folder first to create a real test case, confirm the scan finds exactly them, confirm Extract from archive restores exactly them, confirm Open staging folder / Download archive both work). Flag any DESIGN.md pattern gap you hit (e.g. no existing convention for a two-screen tool flow) — add it to DESIGN.md in the same change if so, per the project's own standing rule.

Flag the new tool in the handoff for README's Key Features list (design side owns that copy) — one sentence on what it does and why it exists.
